boardStatus.physicianSpecialty: No: this is not a physician residency or physician specialty and has no physician specialty board examination.
boardStatus.medicalPhysicsCredential: Separate medical-physics/scientific certifications exist. ABR has medical physics Part 1, specialty Part 2 (including Diagnostic Medical Physics and Nuclear Medical Physics), and Part 3 oral examination. ABSNM administers general and specialty examination components for nuclear-medicine science. Its current Nuclear Medicine Physics & Instrumentation page specifies related graduate education and supervised/practical experience (including dedicated NMPI time); details are not satisfied by this self-study. These are distinct credentials, not physician boards.
boardStatus.institutionalStatement: Boston Children’s program page says graduates are expected to complete board certification in the chosen specialized field through a recognized certifying body, naming ABR, ABSNM or CCPM. The page’s currently described program is 24 months and permits diagnostic or nuclear focus. The ABR states dual diagnostic+nuclear eligibility for a combined 2+1 residency after 36 months; do not infer eligibility for both from the BCH 24-month public description.
boardStatus.eligibilityVerification: Current eligibility is controlled by certifying boards and individual education/training history. A self-study course confers none. CCPM is named by the institution but its route and current eligibility were not independently checked for this curriculum.

boardEligibilityNotice: No eligibility is promised. ABR eligibility requires the board’s education, accredited supervised training and exam requirements; ABR page describes a 2+1/36-month condition for both diagnostic and nuclear specialties. ABSNM has a separate two-part scientific certification exam. Verify current rules directly with the board.

boardStatus: Emory’s current public MIM page describes a combined diagnostic radiology and nuclear medicine residency track, with a stated goal of dual ABR/ABNM board eligibility/certification. The current ABNM rules allow an integrated diagnostic radiology route with 16 months (64 weeks) of nuclear medicine training during a four-year DR residency, subject to all requirements and board review. The ABR and ABNM are separate certifying boards and separate examinations/certifications. ABR exam format is in transition: the ABR page describes computer-based Certifying Exams in 2026–2027 and an oral exam after 2027. Individual eligibility is determined by the boards and accredited training, not by this course.
boardEligibilityNotice: This independent self-study course confers no ABR/ABNM eligibility, ACGME training credit, medical licensure, board certification, supervised interpretation/procedure competence, clinical case logs, NRC authorized-user status, radiation-safety authorization or institutional credentialing. The ABNM/NRC pathway requires supervised hands-on work, specified experience and attestation; online learning cannot supply these. Confirm current eligibility and requirements directly with ABR, ABNM, ACGME, the programme and applicable regulators. No exam pass or readiness is promised.

trackType: Clinical physician fellowship (institutional analogue; independent self-study, not a clinical programme)
boardNames: American Board of Radiology (ABR) — Neuroradiology Subspecialty Exam
boardStatus: ABR offers a distinct neuroradiology subspecialty certification examination for eligible diplomates; not a separate initial physician specialty board. The ABR describes an image-rich, one-day computer-based examination of approximately 180 questions and approximately four hours. Exam guide divides content equally into brain, spine, and head & neck; pediatric cases appear throughout. Current exam format, timing, scoring and requirements can change.
boardEligibilityNotice: ABR information reviewed 2026-10-07 states that applicants need an ABR primary certificate in general radiology/diagnostic radiology or IR/DR; an ACGME- or RCPSC-accredited one-year neuroradiology fellowship; valid medical license; and one year of practice or additional approved training with at least one-third in neuroradiology (or qualifying alternate pathway). Verify directly with ABR. This independent course confers no board eligibility.
